senses.definition: used before a noun, a pronoun, or an -ing form to say that something happens even though this thing might have stopped it
senses.explanation: In spite of is followed by a noun, a pronoun, or an -ing form, never by a clause with a subject and a verb: in spite of the rain, in spite of being tired. For a clause, use although or even though: although it rained. In spite of the fact that is possible but heavy.

examples.text: We went for a walk in spite of the rain.
In spite of everything, they stayed friends.
Omar kept smiling in spite of the pain.
She got the job in spite of having no experience.

items: in spite of the fact that

synonyms.note: despite means the same and is a little more formal; it is never followed by of

compare.note: although introduces a clause with a subject and a verb
even though introduces a clause and is a little stronger

word_family.note: the noun spite means a wish to hurt or annoy someone, a meaning that in spite of has lost

learner_errors.incorrect: in spite of that it rained
learner_errors.note: In spite of cannot introduce a clause; use although, or turn the clause into a noun: in spite of the rain.
Despite is never followed by of; in spite of always is.

adaptation.semantic: In spite of and despite mean the same, and both translate as the one word most languages use for this idea. That word often also works as a conjunction; the English ones do not.
adaptation.grammar: In spite of takes a noun phrase, a pronoun, or an -ing form, never a clause with a subject and a verb: in spite of the rain, in spite of being ill, but although it rained.
adaptation.pronunciation: Said as one unit with the stress on spite; in and of are weak, ɪn and əv.
